title: Review shared CLI, command, dispatch, capability, and tooling support modules
scope: Primary ownership for src/shared CLI, command-registry, dispatch, capability, completions, legacy entrypoint, and tooling-bin helpers assigned to #413 in the shared-module ledger.

summary.overallAssessment: This shared surface is mostly healthy and already acts as the repo's canonical command and CLI contract layer. The main cleanup needs are not broad rewrites. They are targeted: the CLI display family is oversized, dispatch metadata is projected through too many thin layers, and one dispatch runtime-env helper still reaches back into tools/shared for policy resolution. Capability and command metadata should remain centralized here, but a few large files need clearer internal boundaries.

runtimeRisks.reason: This is the runtime display orchestrator for interactive and JSONL progress, and it currently mixes safe-stream guards, task state, render scheduling, task lifecycle, and log routing in one file.
The rendering pipeline is large enough that palette management, layout calculation, and terminal row diffing are hard to reason about as one surface.
CLI flag metadata, API route surface declarations, editor command specs, MCP tool exposure, and runtime capability probing all meet here, so drift in any one sub-surface is expensive.

maintainabilityOnlyNotes.reason: This is a very thin projection over dispatch registry data and likely does not need to stay separate from the dispatch facade long-term.
It is effectively a filtered projection of command-registry data, which means command metadata is being cloned into a second shared projection layer.
The current package-script replacement surface is almost empty and should either stay intentionally tiny or be folded into command-surface reporting if it remains documentation-only.

highestPriorityFollowUps.reason: Separate safe writable-stream handling, task-state mutation, and progress/log emission from the display facade.
Separate palette and theme derivation, layout calculation, and terminal diff rendering into narrower helpers under the display family.
Keep the command table authoritative here, but split registry data from query/projection helpers so completions, help, capabilities, and dispatch do not all pull through one broad module.
Separate static surface specifications from manifest assembly so editor, API, and MCP surface declarations do not drift inside one large runtime file.

It currently depends on tools/shared dict-utils helpers even though the file lives in src/shared. Either move the policy helpers down into src/shared or relocate this wrapper closer to the CLI entrypoint.
Collapse the thin dispatch manifest projection into a smaller dispatch facade so command-registry-derived metadata is not spread across multiple near-empty wrappers.

entries.consumerNotes: Used by auto-policy, capability-gate, config dump, and runtime capability manifest generation as the optional runtime probe surface.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the runtime capability probe facade and avoid duplicating optional-dependency checks elsewhere.

entries.consumerNotes: Single-purpose command-completion generator driven by the canonical command registry.
entries.recommendation: Keep, but preserve the command-registry dependency as read-only projection logic rather than letting shell-specific behavior leak into registry code.

entries.consumerNotes: Owns canonical CLI option schemas for build, bench, service, cache GC, and compare-models flows, plus argument validation helpers.
entries.recommendation: Split static option-set declarations from validation helpers so command metadata stays easy to audit and surface-specific validation logic does not accumulate in one file.

entries.consumerNotes: The main shared yargs wrapper used across CLI and tool surfaces.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the canonical CLI parser facade and resist adding command-specific policy here.

entries.consumerNotes: Low-level ANSI helpers used by retrieval output formatting surfaces.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the ANSI primitive layer and avoid duplicating escape-handling helpers in output formatters.

entries.consumerNotes: Single display facade, but it owns safe writable-stream wrapping, interactive render scheduling, task lifecycle, and JSONL progress/log routing.
entries.recommendation: Split stream safety, state mutation, and task/log event routing into narrower internal modules while keeping createDisplay() as the public facade.

entries.consumerNotes: Focused bar-style and gradient construction helper used only by render.js.
entries.recommendation: Keep as a display-internal bar-rendering module.

entries.consumerNotes: Color math and ANSI composition helper for the display rendering family.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the shared display color primitive layer.

entries.consumerNotes: Owns progress-specific calculations such as overall progress and per-task extras.
entries.recommendation: Keep separate from raw rendering so progress math remains isolated and testable.

entries.consumerNotes: Large renderer that mixes palette derivation, layout, animated bar selection, and terminal diff writes.
entries.recommendation: Split theme/palette resolution, layout computation, and row-diff rendering into narrower helpers under the display family.

entries.consumerNotes: Small adapter for terminal-kit normalization and terminal width resolution.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the terminal adapter boundary for the display family.

entries.consumerNotes: Formatting and ANSI-safe text helpers used throughout the display family.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the text-formatting helper layer for CLI display behavior.

entries.consumerNotes: Small compatibility helper for surfaces that accept optional display task factories.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the no-op task fallback rather than reimplementing null-task objects at callsites.

entries.consumerNotes: Protocol definition used by CLI display, bench, TUI supervisor, and runtime capability reporting.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the authoritative progress protocol contract and avoid copying event names into local modules.

entries.consumerNotes: Line decoder for progress protocol streams used by bench and TUI supervisor code.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the shared progress-line decoding helper.

entries.consumerNotes: Protects JSON-mode stdout contracts in setup and install tooling.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the stdout JSON contract guard rather than embedding output-contract checks in each tool.

entries.consumerNotes: Small documentation and audit helper for package-script replacement metadata.
entries.recommendation: Keep intentionally tiny, but do not let it become a second command-registry surface unless package-script replacements meaningfully expand.

entries.consumerNotes: Canonical command table used by the CLI entrypoint, completions, command-alias reporting, dispatch registry, capability manifest, and command-surface audit tooling.
entries.recommendation: Keep this as the single source of truth, but split the static registry data from query/projection helpers so dispatch, help, and completion logic do not all depend on one broad mixed module.

entries.consumerNotes: Only the CLI entrypoint uses this shared wrapper, and it currently depends on tools/shared dict-utils helpers plus runtime-envelope logic.
entries.recommendation: Either move the dict-utils runtime-policy helpers down into src/shared or relocate this wrapper closer to the CLI entrypoint so src/shared does not depend on tools/shared for dispatch env resolution.

entries.consumerNotes: Very thin projection layer over dispatch registry data for tooling visibility.
entries.recommendation: Merge into a smaller dispatch facade or collapse with registry helpers so dispatch metadata is not spread across multiple near-empty wrappers.

entries.consumerNotes: Filtered command-registry projection that clones dispatch-listed entries and rebuilds path/id maps.
entries.recommendation: Collapse projection logic closer to command-registry or a single dispatch facade so metadata cloning is minimized.

entries.consumerNotes: Small command-path matcher over the dispatch registry.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the dispatch request resolver, but leave it thin and data-driven.

entries.consumerNotes: Small compatibility helper for warning suppression and migration messaging from legacy entrypoints.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the legacy-entrypoint compatibility shim until those wrappers are fully retired.

entries.consumerNotes: Capability manifest builder that assembles runtime probes, CLI flag sets, API routes, MCP tool exposure, TUI capabilities, and editor command specs.
entries.recommendation: Split static surface declarations from manifest assembly so editor/API/MCP/CLI sub-surfaces can evolve without growing one broad runtime metadata file.

entries.consumerNotes: Shared platform-aware search path expansion for command resolution and tooling utilities.
entries.recommendation: Keep as the canonical tooling-bin search helper and avoid reimplementing platform-specific PATH augmentation in callers.
